proof:
# A general coefficient in the dominated-density centroid inequality

Let B be a convex body in R^d, d>=1, let 0<=eta<=1_B dx, and let L>=2
be real. If g is the centroid of 1_B dx+L eta, then every closed halfspace
H containing g satisfies

    |B intersect H|+eta(H)
       >= (gamma_d/L)(|B|+L eta(B)).                   (1)

This is a continuous auxiliary statement. A representation of arbitrary
mixed volume by such a dominated target has not been proved or assumed.

Normalize |B| to one in the measure calculations. Write p for the base
cap probability, e for eta's cap mass, and a for eta's total mass. The
cap-root Jensen and two-interval bathtub proof in
`candidate d4ddcd5e9c4567f8` now gives, with s=1/d and
r=d/(d+1),

    (1+La)p^s >= r[1+L e^(1+s)+L(p+a-e)^(1+s)-L p^(1+s)].

The centroid lies in int B and hence 0<p<1. Put

    U=1/p, E=e/p, Q=(p+a-e)/p,
    phi(t)=t-r t^(1+s), c=1/(d+1), k=1/gamma_d.

Dividing the preceding inequality gives exactly

    phi(U)+L phi(Q)+L phi(E)>=L c.                    (2)

The desired conclusion is equivalent to

    D=U+LQ-L(k-1)E <= L(1+k).                        (3)

For tau=1/d, the elementary scalar Fenchel inequality used in the cited
proof gives

    phi(U)+L phi(Q)+L phi(E)+tau D
       <= (1+L)c(1+tau)^(d+1)
          +L c[1-tau(k-1)]_+^(d+1).

Combining with (2), it suffices to show

    Ld[1-(k-1)/d]_+^(d+1)
       <=L(2d+1)-(d+1)k.                             (4)

After division by L, the right side increases with L. For L=2, (4) is
exactly the already proved scalar inequality (10) in the cited note.
Therefore (4) holds for every real L>=2. This proves (3) and (1). All
normalization, centroid-membership, and closed-boundary details are the
same as in that proof; eta is absolutely continuous and no boundary mass
is lost.

There is a simple obstruction to a naive mixed-integer application. In
one integer dimension, if one proposes a target 1_B dx+eta in a chosen
fiber, dominated in every containing cap by the original mixed measure,
then the two vertical caps force

    eta(B)<=min(mass strictly left,mass strictly right).

To make |B|+2eta(B) equal the original total mass would require those two
strict-side masses to be equal. A marginal median need not have that
equality. Thus the continuous theorem does not by itself supply a general
mixed-integer representation or an integer-center selection rule.
